issues.problem: "HYUNDAI PLANS A SUPERCOMPUTER" calls the project a machine. Only ZDNet Korea uses the word, and it says "슈퍼컴퓨팅 거점" (supercomputing base), and calls the project a "하이퍼스케일 데이터센터" (hyperscale data center). The Korea Times says only "AI data center". Neither article says Hyundai will build a supercomputer.
issues.fix: Use the article's wording, e.g. ["HYUNDAI PLANS AN AI", "**SUPERCOMPUTING BASE**"] (check the render fits), or drop the word: "HYUNDAI PLANS AN" / "**AI DATA CENTER**". Update hook_options[0] and hook_pick_reason to match. Also change the caption question "Should carmakers build their own AI supercomputers?" to "Should carmakers build their own AI supercomputing bases?" or "...their own AI data centers?"

issues.problem: "Financing is still being coordinated with Korea Development Bank." ZDNet Korea says: "산업은행 등과 체결한 업무협약을 바탕으로 금융지원 방안도 조율 중이다" (financing support is being coordinated based on a business agreement signed with the Korea Development Bank and others). The post drops "and others", drops the signed agreement, and implies KDB alone is the counterparty. It also does not say who KDB is (CLAUDE.md requires a one-line description for lesser-known institutions).
issues.fix: Replace with: "Financing support is still being worked out, based on an agreement with Korea Development Bank, a South Korean state-run bank, and others." (Drop "state-run" if you want to keep strictly to the article; the exception for plain, widely known background allows it.) Shorten the 9 trillion won sentence if the slide overflows. Same reasoning for facts[8]: its note is accurate, but the slide must match it.
